original_question: Suppose that φ is an automorphism of a finite soluble group G, and let r be the(Prüfer) rank of the fixed-point subgroup CG(φ). Is the Fitting height of G bounded terms of |φ| and r? This is known to be true in the case where |φ| is a product of at most two prime powers(B. Hartley, Preprint, 1994, https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress. com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/hartley94-prepr-mims.pdf). An affirmative answer to this question would imply an affirmative answer to 13.8(b).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.67 in the 21st issue (2026), New Problems: whether the Fitting height of a finite soluble group G is bounded solely in terms of the order of an automorphism φ and the (Prüfer) rank of its fixed-point subgroup C_G(φ). The paper also notes that an affirmative answer would imply an affirmative answer to 13.8(b). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s official formulation. It has the right setting (finite soluble group G with an automorphism φ), the right invariant (the (Prüfer) rank of C_G(φ)), the right target quantity (the Fitting height of G), and it preserves the two context sentences that the paper itself appends: the known special case when |φ| is a product of at most two prime powers, and the implication for 13.8(b). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, the notation C_G(φ) should be expanded as the fixed-point subgroup of φ; in 21.67 the notation is used without local explanation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

The usual quantifier behind “bounded in terms of |φ| and r” should be stated explicitly, namely: does there exist a function f such that h(G) ≤ f(|φ|, r) for every finite soluble group G and automorphism φ? Problem 21.67 asks the boundedness question in shorthand form. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

If maximum self-containment is desired, the standard term “(Prüfer) rank” should be spelled out, since 21.67 names it but does not define it locally. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
Likewise, if one introduces notation h(G), one should say explicitly that this denotes the Fitting height of the finite soluble group G. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

The raw URL of Hartley’s preprint is not part of the mathematical statement itself; in the paper it appears only as bibliographic background for the known special case. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Let G be a finite soluble group and let φ be an automorphism of G. Let C_G(φ) = {g ∈ G : g^φ = g} be the fixed-point subgroup, and let r be its (Prüfer) rank. Does there exist a function f : N × N → N such that the Fitting height h(G) satisfies h(G) ≤ f(|φ|, r)?
justification: The nearest official target is exactly 21.67, not a broader neighboring problem. Your draft matches 21.67 almost verbatim and even keeps the paper’s own two follow-up remarks. By contrast, 19.43 is a different and weaker question, asking for a bound in terms of |φ| and |C_G(φ)|, and it is marked solved in the current version; 21.65 asks only for a bounded-index subgroup of bounded Fitting height; and 21.66 replaces a single automorphism by a nilpotent automorphism group A. So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is to state 21.67 cleanly and self-containedly, without drifting to those adjacent variants. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
